deals.headline: Angers SCO takes a 35-year emphyteutic lease on Stade Raymond-Kopa from the City
deals.summary: The club and the City of Angers signed a 35-year emphyteutic lease on the municipal stadium, giving the club scope to fund works; the Saint-Léonard stand was rebuilt from 2019 and opened for 2022-23, taking capacity to 19,800. No price or rent is published.

stadium_owner.detail: The City of Angers has owned the ground since 1957; in May 2018 the club and the City signed a 35-year emphyteutic lease (bail emphytéotique) that lets the club carry out works, and the club rebuilt the Saint-Léonard stand (opened 2022). The club's organisation page describes the stadium built under Saïd Chabane as its own property.

name: Angers SCO (Angers Sporting Club de l'Ouest)
notes: Revenue and P&L facts are the DNCG 2024/25 individual club accounts (perimeter: SA + Association + Financière Le Buron + subsidiaries, K EUR; Angers was in Ligue 1 that season); 'revenue' is total non-transfer earnings, excluding a EUR 12.5m profit on player trading; financial debts EUR 10.9m and cash EUR 7.0m, but no net-debt figure is published. The club says 2025-26 player sales (EUR 20m, EUR 38m including Sidiki Cherif's permanent move) let it divide its debt by five, without giving amounts. The holding that carries the 99.1% is not named by the source; the register shows Chabane's Société Financière Cosnelle presiding Financière Le Buron, which is inside the DNCG perimeter. Chabane bought the club in 2011 for about USD 1.8m (Front Office Sports) / about EUR 1.7m (Sportune), before this file's 2015 deal window. Sale talk is not recorded as a deal or valuation: the 2022 sale (reported at USD 84m) collapsed; in September 2025 press reported a refused EUR 30m offer and an asking price of about EUR 50m, with the owner citing more than EUR 67m of non-sporting assets. Governance moved in 2025-26 from a board of directors to a supervisory board and management board. Attendance is the club's own 'more than 13,100' average for 2024-25 (recorded as 13,100; the club called it the second-highest in its history). No shirt sponsor named on a club page found; no social or honours figures recorded.

owners.evidence: qui détient via sa holding 99,1 % des actions du club angevin
owners.name: Saïd Chabane (via his holding company; Cosnelle group)

ownership_summary: Owned since 2011 by Saïd Chabane, head of the Sarthe agri-food group Cosnelle, who holds 99.1% of the shares through his holding company and chairs the supervisory board; day-to-day management sits with a management board chaired by Jérôme Negroni. No institutional investor is on the register. A 2022 sale (reported at USD 84m) collapsed, and in 2025 the owner was reported to have turned down a EUR 30m offer while the club remains open to a buyer.
